issues.t: Engine oil sludge buildup
issues.sym: Blue smoke, an oil pressure light, ticking or knocking from the engine, or oil disappearing between changes.
issues.why: This engine can form thick, gel-like sludge inside when oil changes are stretched out, which blocks oil passages and starves bearings and the valvetrain. Toyota acknowledged the problem with a special coverage policy.
issues.next: Stop driving if the oil light comes on or the engine knocks. Have the oil pickup and passages inspected, and keep oil changes on a short schedule from then on.

issues.t: Alarm wiring connector can make the engine stall (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or electrical items cut in and out without warning.
issues.why: Terminals in a connector for the theft alarm system were faulty and could lose contact intermittently. Toyota recalled these vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for completed recall work. If the van stalls or flickers electrically, have it towed in rather than driven.

issues.t: Front subframe welds may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks or knocks from the front end over bumps, or the front wheels feeling loose or shifting.
issues.why: Some front subframes were not welded properly at the factory and could crack or separate over time. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. If the front end clunks or feels loose, stop driving and have the subframe inspected.

issues.t: Spare tire carrier cable rusting through (recall)
issues.sym: A rattle or clunk from under the rear of the van, or the spare tire hanging low.
issues.why: The cable that holds the spare under the van can corrode from road salt and let the spare drop onto the road. Toyota recalled 1998-2010 vans and later added 2004-2011 vans in a second campaign.
issues.next: Look under the rear to see how the spare sits and check your VIN for both recalls, especially in salt-belt states.

issues.t: Power steering rack leaking
issues.sym: Wet steering rack boots, a power steering reservoir that keeps dropping, groaning when turning, or heavy, notchy steering.
issues.why: The seals inside the steering rack on this generation commonly wear and leak fluid. Running it low can also wear out the pump.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and look for wet boots behind the front wheels. Have the rack replaced if it is leaking steadily.

issues.t: Shift lever can leave Park without the brake pressed (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter moves out of Park without your foot on the brake.
issues.why: A fault in the shift lock system could let the lever be moved out of Park without the brake applied, raising the chance of the van rolling. Toyota ran two recalls covering different years in this range.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Until fixed, always set the parking brake and keep your foot on the brake when shifting.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley can separate and throw the power steering belt (recall)
issues.sym: A squeal or slapping noise from the engine, followed by suddenly heavy steering.
issues.why: The rubber bond in the crankshaft pulley may not have been made correctly, so the outer ring can shift and throw the power steering belt. Toyota recalled these vans.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. If the steering suddenly gets heavy or a belt noise appears, pull over safely and have the van towed.

issues.t: Power liftgate struts wearing out early (recall)
issues.sym: The rear hatch will not stay up, drifts down, or the power liftgate strains and stops.
issues.why: The gas struts that hold up the heavy liftgate can lose pressure early, so the gate may come down on someone. Toyota recalled 2004-2006 vans, and worn struts remain a common repair on this generation.
issues.next: Check for the recall and replace weak struts as a pair. Do not stand under a hatch that will not hold itself up.

issues.t: Loose floor carpet can catch the gas pedal (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal feels sticky or does not return fully when you lift off.
issues.why: A carpet retaining clip was missing on some vans, so the carpet could slide and interfere with the accelerator. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and make sure nothing under the pedal can bunch up. If the pedal sticks, shift to Neutral and brake firmly.

issues.t: Middle-row shoulder belt can bind (recall)
issues.sym: A second-row shoulder belt is hard to pull out or does not retract smoothly.
issues.why: The belt webbing could catch in its trim bezel, which may stop it restraining a passenger properly in a crash. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Have the recall done before carrying passengers in that seat.

issues.t: Accessory seat heater wiring can short and burn (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell, a seat that gets too hot, or a heated seat that stops working.
issues.why: On vans fitted with accessory (non-factory) seat heaters, sitting on the cushion could damage the heater wiring and cause a short, with a risk of burns or fire. Toyota ran two recalls for this.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater and have the van checked for both recalls if it has an add-on heated seat.

issues.t: Power sliding door cable and motor failures
issues.sym: The sliding door grinds or clicks, stops partway, reverses, or will only work by hand.
issues.why: The door cables fray and the motors, latches and actuators wear out from heavy use. Toyota extended warranty coverage on door parts for some of these vans.
issues.next: Have the door system inspected before a frayed cable snaps, and ask the dealer whether any extended coverage applies to your van.

issues.t: Power sliding door can open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: A sliding door pops open or tries to open while the van is moving.
issues.why: If the door is blocked from opening when commanded, the motor's protection logic could leave the latch released so the door opens later while moving. Toyota recalled these vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Until fixed, keep the power door system switched off and make sure the doors are latched before driving.

issues.t: Rubber VVT oil line can burst
issues.sym: Oil spraying or dripping at the back of the engine, a burning oil smell, or the oil light coming on while driving.
issues.why: Early versions of this engine used an oil feed line to the variable valve timing with a rubber section that can crack and suddenly dump the engine's oil. Toyota later switched to an all-metal line and extended coverage on it.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, stop the engine right away. Ask a shop whether your van still has the rubber line and replace it with the updated metal part.

issues.t: Water pump leaking coolant
issues.sym: Pink crust near the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or the coolant level dropping.
issues.why: The water pump seal and bearing commonly wear out on this engine before other cooling parts do.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and have the pump replaced if it is seeping. Do not drive if the temperature gauge climbs.

issues.t: Front right drive shaft may break (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from the front, vibration, or a sudden loss of drive.
issues.why: Some right front drive shafts were not heat-treated properly and could break. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. If you hear a new clunk or lose drive, stop and have the van towed.

issues.t: Brake light switch bracket can cause dragging brakes (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights staying on, a hot brake smell, or the van feeling like the brakes are partly applied.
issues.why: The parking brake pedal could bend the bracket holding the brake light switch, which can keep the brakes slightly applied. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Check the recall status and have the brakes checked if you smell hot brakes or the brake lights stay on.

issues.t: Fuel delivery pipe may leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell from the engine bay or wet spots near the engine.
issues.why: A fuel delivery pipe on some vans could leak fuel near hot engine parts, creating a fire risk. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, do not drive the van. Have it towed and check the VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Damaged shift cable may select the wrong gear (recall)
issues.sym: The gear shown on the dash does not match the shifter, or the van moves when it should be in Park.
issues.why: The shift cable sleeve could be damaged, so the transmission may not end up in the gear selected and the van could roll away. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. Until then, always set the parking brake and check that the van is truly in Park before getting out.

issues.t: Front seat belt height adjuster may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; the shoulder belt anchor may feel loose or shift.
issues.why: The front seat belt height adjusters on some vans could tear or separate in a crash. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have it done promptly.

issues.t: Brake booster vacuum pump may fail (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels hard and the van takes much more effort to stop.
issues.why: Some vacuum pumps for the brake booster were machined incorrectly and could fail, removing power assist for the brakes. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Check the recall status. If the pedal turns hard, press firmly, pull over safely, and have the van towed.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump may fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light, power loss, stalling while driving, or a no-start.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump impeller can swell and rub, cutting fuel delivery. Toyota recalled affected vans in two campaigns.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both fuel pump recalls. If the engine stumbles or stalls, get off the road and have it towed rather than restarting repeatedly.

issues.t: Front door welds may affect side airbag sensing (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom; sometimes an airbag warning light.
issues.why: Welds in the passenger front door could interfere with the side impact sensor, which may affect how airbags deploy. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have it repaired promptly.

issues.t: Brakes lurch or briefly release at low speed
issues.sym: While slowing to a stop, the brakes feel like they let go for a moment or the van surges forward before stopping.
issues.why: Owners report the problem during the hand-off between regenerative braking from the hybrid system and the regular hydraulic brakes, often over bumps or at low speed.
issues.next: Report it to the dealer and NHTSA, ask for any brake software updates, and leave extra stopping room until it is checked.

issues.t: Passenger seat occupant sensor may short (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag OFF light stays on with an adult seated, or an airbag warning light appears.
issues.why: A short circuit in the front passenger occupant classification sensor may keep the passenger airbag from deploying. Toyota recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done, and keep children in the back seat until the sensor is replaced.

issues.t: Stability control may not turn back on after restart (recall)
issues.sym: The VSC OFF light stays on after you restart a van in which you had switched stability control off.
issues.why: Software in the skid control computer may not re-enable stability control on the next start, which does not meet federal rules. Toyota recalled affected vans.
issues.next: Have the software update done. Until then, check that the VSC OFF light is out after each start.

issues.t: Second-row seat belt webbing guide may be wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom; the outer second-row belt may look like it rubs or routes oddly.
issues.why: An incorrect webbing guide may be fitted on outboard second-row belts in 8-passenger vans, which can make the belt easier to tear in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have it done before using those seats.

issues.t: Third-row seatback bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A third-row seatback that feels loose, rattles, or shifts.
issues.why: Bolts holding the third-row seatbacks may not have been tightened at the factory, so the seat may not hold a passenger or child seat properly in a crash.
issues.next: Have the dealer tighten the bolts under the recall before carrying passengers in the third row.

issues.t: Oil leak from the lower oil pan
issues.sym: Oil drips on the driveway under the middle of the engine and the oil level falls between changes, often with a burnt smell.
issues.why: The sealer between the upper and lower oil pan sections can let go, so oil seeps from the seam.
issues.next: Have the pan reseal done before the level gets low; keep checking the oil until it is fixed.

issues.t: Knocking noise from the engine vacuum pump at idle
issues.sym: A knock or tap from the front of the engine at idle that you hear best with the hood up, steady rather than rising with speed.
issues.why: The brake vacuum pump driven off the engine can become noisy inside.
issues.next: Have a technician confirm the noise is the vacuum pump and not an internal engine problem before any big repair is quoted.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failing catalytic converter
issues.sym: Check engine light with catalyst efficiency codes, sometimes a sulfur smell or a dull feel under acceleration.
issues.why: The material inside one of the converters can break down, so the sensors no longer see it cleaning the exhaust properly.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the converter checked; get it done before an emissions test and while any extended coverage still applies.

issues.t: Transmission side cover fluid leak
issues.sym: Red or brown fluid drips near the front wheel area and a faint hot oil smell after driving.
issues.why: The sealed side cover on the automatic transmission can weep fluid at its joint.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and the cover resealed; running a transmission low on fluid can ruin it.

issues.t: Noise from the all-wheel drive rear coupling
issues.sym: A humming, groaning or binding noise from under the rear of the van, most noticeable in tight turns or parking lots.
issues.why: The coupling at the front of the rear differential that sends power to the back wheels can wear or behave abnormally.
issues.next: Have the rear driveline inspected; it is not an emergency but it gets worse and the parts are not cheap.

issues.t: Front door window can come out of its channel
issues.sym: A bang or grinding while raising or lowering a front window, then glass that sits crooked, rattles or will not move.
issues.why: The glass can separate from the channel that guides it in the door.
issues.next: Stop using that window and have the door glass reattached, because loose glass can drop into the door and break.

issues.t: Musty smell from the vents after water gets in
issues.sym: A damp, musty or sour smell when the fan comes on, often worse after rain or in humid weather.
issues.why: Water that gets into the cabin or a blocked air conditioning drain keeps carpet and ductwork damp, and mold grows there.
issues.next: Have the drain cleared and the source of the water found, then the carpet dried and the system treated; mostly a comfort issue but it keeps coming back if the leak stays.

issues.t: Front brake pedal pulsates under light braking
issues.sym: A shudder or pulsing through the brake pedal and steering wheel when braking gently from higher speeds.
issues.why: The front brake rotors wear unevenly, so their surface no longer runs true against the pads.
issues.next: Have the front rotors measured and resurfaced or replaced; it is a comfort and control issue, not an immediate safety failure.

issues.t: Second-row seat backs may not stay locked in a crash (recall 26V-690)
issues.sym: Nothing obvious in normal use; the seat back looks and feels normal but may not hold if the van is hit.
issues.why: On seven-passenger vans the second-row seat backs can fail to stay secured in a collision, because the restraint system software and, on some vans, the seat backs themselves are not to specification.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked and let the dealer load the updated airbag-system software, or replace the seat backs where that applies, at no charge.
